title: Progressive GPU-spill with token-level shedding and heterogeneous-model fallback for OOM resilience
creator: Asha Patel
description: Design and implement a layered OOM mitigation strategy that reduces hard failures by: (1) opportunistically spilling large KV cache blocks to host RAM/NVMe with bounded latency impact, (2) token-level progressive shedding for high-concurrency tails, and (3) automatic heterogeneous-model fallback (smaller quantized model variants or CPU-safe paths) when GPU memory pressure persists. Aim to eliminate hard OOMs in 95% of observed peak scenarios while keeping P95 latency degradation under 30% for affected requests.
acceptance_criteria: Service no longer returns CUDA OOM errors for synthetic and historical peak traces used in our 2025 incident corpus in 95% of runs
When spill occurs, 90th percentile end-to-end latency increase for spilled requests <= 30% and P99 increase <= 2x compared to baseline
Progressive token-shedding produces deterministic, auditable outputs: shedding levels documented and reproducible via unit tests
Fallback switch to hetero-model variant completes and serves consistent outputs (semantically similar) with automated telemetry flags
Observability: dashboard shows leak-free spill counts, host-swapping time, KV-snapshot sizes, and per-model fallback rate; alerts fire when fallback rate > 1% over 5m
tasks: Prototype spill format: compressed KV block layout + sequence-numbered chunking for partial restore
Implement async spill-to-host pipeline with backpressure tokens and priority admission
Add token-level progressive shedding hook to serving runtime with configurable policies (truncate, summary, soft-stop)
Integrate hetero-fallback decision engine that evaluates memory pressure, latency budget, and quality delta
End-to-end tests: replay historical production traces with injected memory pressure and validate behavior
Create observability surfaces: grafana panels, new Prometheus metrics, and alerting rules
Document runbook and add automated incident mitigation playbook for on-call
notes: 2026-03-02: Kickoff meeting. Agreed to avoid synchronous host-blocking spills; must be async with bounded memory reservation.
2026-03-04: Design review feedback from Lina Morales: prefer chunked compressed spill to avoid fragmentation and allow partial restores for low-latency cold-prefixes.
2026-03-06: Trade-off decision: support two shedding strategies (truncate suffix vs. soft-summary) with runtime-config flags per route. Chosen to enable per-customer policy without code change.
2026-03-07: Security note from Security team: spills must be encrypted at rest when written to NVMe in Private deployments. Added KMS integration task.
2026-03-09: Initial prototype showed 40% P95 latency uplift on small-GPU machines when spill-to-host used naive memcpy; next iteration will use pinned buffers + async IO.
2026-03-11: UX sync with Console team: expose fallback_reason tags and shedding_level on traces. Console will show per-request degradation level.
2026-03-12: PR created for async spill pipeline: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/789. Needs perf benchmarks and integration tests before merge.
implementation_plan: Phase 1: implement compressed chunked spill and async writer with pinned host buffers (2 sprints). Phase 2: integrate token-shedding hook and test policies (1 sprint). Phase 3: hetero-fallback engine + rollout gating and canary (1 sprint). Phase 4: observability + runbook + customer opt-in controls (1 sprint). Rollout via canary hosts in dedicated pool then broader runtime rollout with automatic rollback on error thresholds.
rollback_plan: Feature gated with runtime flag. If rollout causes client-visible regression (fallback_rate > 5% or error_rate spike), disable spill pipeline and revert to previous config. Emergency hotfix: force-disabled hetero-fallback and token-shedding via runtime override API. Postmortem and tune chunk-size/IO threadpool before next attempt.
